title: The Final Cut
full_review:
"The Final Cut" (Lions Gate) is a gloomy sci-fi thriller set in a future where humans can have devices called "Zoe chips" implanted in utero which record their entire lives. These chips are downloaded at death and edited into sanitized memorial films called "rememories" to be shown at their funerals.

An impassive Robin Williams plays Alan Hackman, a "cutter" whose proficiency at cleaning up the scandalous memories of his well-heeled clientele has made him the most sought-after editor in the business.

Haunted by a dark secret of his own, Hackman is hired by the wealthy widow of a corrupt, high-ranking Zoe executive named Bannister, who, among his many sins, sexually molested his own young daughter. The job puts Hackman at odds with a former associate (Jim Caviezel) -- now working for an anti-Zoe group -- who will do whatever it takes to get his hands on Bannister's memory implant in the hopes of bringing down the Zoe corporation by exposing Bannister's crimes.

Directed by Omar Naim and clearly inspired by Francis Ford Coppola's "The Conversation" (1974), "The Final Cut" raises intriguing ethical questions but is weighed down by its cheerless performances and slumberous pacing.

Due to brief violence, an implied sexual encounter and some crude language and profanity, the USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
